import: Loads a module (another file or library). You can give it a short name with as, as in import numpy as np
from: Loads only part of a module. from datetime import date
as: Gives another name to something imported, or something opened with with
def: Makes a function. After def name(arguments):, write the body indented
return: Returns the function's answer and ends the function
class: Makes a class (a blueprint bundling data and functions)
self: Inside a method, refers to "this object itself". Written as the method's first argument
__init__: The method called first when an object is made (the constructor). Sets the initial values
__name__: The current file's name. It is '__main__' only when the file is run directly
__str__: A special method that decides how the object looks when turned into text with print() or str()
__lt__: A special method that defines comparison with < (used when sorting)
super: Calls the parent class. super().__init__() runs the parent's initialization
if: Runs only when the condition is true
elif: When the previous if was not true, checks another condition (else if)
else: Runs when none of the conditions matched
for: Takes the contents of a container one at a time and repeats
while: Repeats while the condition is true
in: In for, "one at a time from..."; in a condition, "whether it is in..."
or: True when at least one is true
is: Whether two things are the same object. Used to check for None, as in x is None
continue: Skips the rest of this round of the loop and goes to the next
pass: Does nothing (put where the grammar needs something)
match: Branches by the shape of a value (from Python 3.10). Combined with case
case: Inside match, one shape to match. case _: means "everything else"
try: Wraps code where an error may occur
except: What to do when an error occurs inside try. You can specify the kind, as in except ValueError:
finally: Always runs at the end, whether or not an error occurred
with: Opens a file or the like and closes it automatically when done
lambda: Makes a small unnamed function on the spot. lambda x: x * 2
del: Deletes a variable or an element of a list
print.sep: The text put between several values (default: one space)
print.end: The text added at the end (default: a newline)
input: Reads one line from the keyboard (returned as a string)
len: The length (number of elements or characters)
range: Makes a run of integers. range(5) is 0–4, range(1, 6) is 1–5
list: Makes a list (an ordered, changeable container)
set: Makes a set (a container with no duplicates)
int: An integer. int("3") turns a string into an integer
float: A decimal (floating-point number). float("2.5") turns a string into a decimal
str: A string. str(3) turns a number into a string
type: Checks the type of a value
isinstance: Checks whether a value is of a given type
round: Rounds (to the nearest even number at .5). round(x, 1) gives 1 decimal place
sorted: Returns a new sorted list. key= sets what to sort by, reverse=True sorts largest first
sorted.key: A function that decides what to sort by. key=lambda c: c["milk"]
enumerate: Takes out a number and an item as a pair, one at a time
enumerate.start: The number to start counting from (default: 0)
zip: Takes items at the same position from several containers as pairs
open: Opens a file. "r" reads, "w" writes (overwrites), "a" appends
open.encoding: The character encoding. For Japanese, use encoding="utf-8"
open.newline: How newlines are handled. Use newline="" when writing csv
append: Adds to the end of a list
insert: Adds at a given position in a list. insert(0, x) adds at the front
pop: Takes an item out of a list and removes it (the last one if no position is given)
remove: Finds that value in a list and removes it
items: Takes out a dictionary's key–value pairs one at a time
keys: The list of a dictionary's keys
values: The list of a dictionary's values
get: Gets a value from a dictionary. If the key is missing, returns None (or the second argument)
strip: Removes spaces and newlines at both ends
split: Splits a string at a separator into a list
join: Joins the strings in a list with text in between. ", ".join(names)
format: Puts values into a string (f"..." f-strings do the same)
math: A module of math functions (sqrt, pi, sin and so on)
pi: π, the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter
sin: Sine. The angle is in radians
os: A module for handling the OS (files, folders, environment variables)
os.path: Handles file paths (location strings). os.path.join joins them correctly
environ: A dictionary of environment variables. os.environ.get("NAME", default)
sys: A module for information about Python itself
argv: The list of arguments when run as a command. sys.argv[1] is the first
sleep: Waits for the given number of seconds
monotonic: Seconds on a clock that never goes backwards. Used to measure elapsed time
json: A module for reading and writing JSON files
dump: Writes to a file as JSON
load: Reads a JSON file into dictionaries and lists
dump.ensure_ascii: False writes Japanese and other non-ASCII text as it is
dump.indent: The indent width. Makes the JSON easy to read
csv: A module for reading and writing CSV (comma-separated) files
writer: Makes a tool for writing CSV
DictReader: Reads CSV one row at a time as a dictionary (header → value)
timedelta: A length of time (days, hours). Can be added to or subtracted from dates
dataclass: A marker (@dataclass) that lets you write data-holding classes briefly
field: Settings for a data class field. field(default_factory=list) makes an empty list the default
default_factory: A function that makes the default value. Used when the default is changeable, such as a list
glob: Returns a list of files matching a file name pattern (*.py and so on)
Traceback: The display of the chain of calls when an error occurs. The last line is the error itself
ZeroDivisionError: The error when you divide by 0
ValueError: The error when a value is wrong (int("abc") and so on)
KeyboardInterrupt: The exception raised when you stop with Ctrl + C
KeyError: The error when you use a key that is not in the dictionary
IndexError: The error when you use a position outside the list
TypeError: The error when types do not match (adding a string and a number and so on)
FileNotFoundError: The error when a file cannot be found
venv: A Python virtual environment (a per-project place for libraries)
pip: The tool for installing Python libraries
